title: Red Lentil Soup
subtitle: Spiced and silky Middle Eastern bowl
excerpt: A richly spiced soup built on red lentils that break down into a smooth, velvety texture without any blending. Finished with lemon juice and fresh parsley, it is warming, filling, and naturally vegan.
sourceNotes: Red lentil soup is a staple across Turkey, Lebanon, and Egypt, where it is known variously as mercimek corbasi or shorbat adas. The spice profile and the finishing squeeze of lemon are characteristic of the Levantine and Ottoman cooking traditions.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes very well. Cool completely, then freeze in portions for up to 3 months.
recipe.batchNotes: An excellent batch-cook option. Make a large pot and portion into containers.

content.text: Red lentils need no soaking and dissolve into the broth as they cook, creating a naturally thick soup. Rinse them well before adding to keep the broth clear. Add the lemon juice only at the end; acid added early can prevent the lentils from softening properly.
Heat the olive oil in the saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion and carrot and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until the onion is soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and chilli flakes. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring, until fragrant.
Add the tomato puree and stir for 30 seconds. Then add the tinned tomatoes, rinsed lentils, and stock.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils have completely broken down and the soup is thick.
Squeeze in the lemon juice, taste, and season generously with salt. Add a splash more stock if the soup is thicker than you prefer.
Ladle into bowls and scatter over the parsley. Serve with warm flatbread if you like.

items.symptom: Lentils have not broken down after 25 minutes.
items.cause: Old lentils can take longer, or the heat was too low.
items.fix: Cook for 10 more minutes on a slightly higher heat.

items.cause: Too much stock was used, or lentils were old and did not swell properly.
items.fix: Simmer uncovered for 5 to 10 more minutes to reduce.

items.cause: Not enough lemon or salt was added at the end.
items.fix: Add more lemon juice and salt; taste again before serving.
